clue.text: Christmas present causing undisguised anger

parts.note: undisguised speech is frank, open and candid
to incense someone is to anger them

explanation.surface: A Christmas gift that makes someone openly furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas present' points to the gifts the Magi brought to the infant Jesus: gold, myrrh and this resin.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic gum resin was one of the three gifts of the wise men in the Nativity story.

clue.text: Intended getting hold of new money

indicators.note: the betrothed person grips the next letter, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: one's intended is the person one is engaged to marry, a fiance

explanation.surface: A betrothed partner grabbing hold of some fresh cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means funds or monetary resources, as in raising the capital for a project.

clue.text: In general (I quote) it will divide exactly

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words general and I quote

explanation.surface: A speaker, quoting themselves, generalises about something that divides evenly.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'generAL I QUOTe'; the brackets are only punctuation in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics an aliquot part is a factor that goes into a quantity a whole number of times without remainder.

clue.text: Broken set repaired for part of pavement

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A broken set of things has been fixed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'repaired' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The kerb (US curb) is the raised stone edge of a pavement, built from these blocks.

clue.text: The sound of drum in mother-of-pearl

indicators.note: the word for the drum is said aloud and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a naker is an old word for a kettledrum

explanation.surface: Drumming heard inside a shell's lustrous lining.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAKER is a medieval kettledrum, an obscure word the clue relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is the iridescent lining of oyster and other shells, also called mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: He'll put up with English cleric

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest, a cleric

explanation.surface: Someone will tolerate an English clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'with' is only a link: the definition is 'He'll put up', someone who builds.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is one who raises or constructs things, such as scaffolding.

clue.text: A target to aim at — runner joins race leaders in lap eight

parts.note: a ski is a runner that glides over snow
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

indicators.note: the opening letters of the words lap and eight are taken

explanation.surface: A runner pulls level with the front pack on the eighth lap.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the famous Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: In ninepins or skittles, the bowler aims to knock down the wooden pins, so each pin is a target.

clue.text: A trick doesn't form standard equipment for business

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick that won't take shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's stock-in-trade is the goods and tools it routinely needs to carry on its work.

clue.text: Port with more zest

explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan harbour city; tangier is the comparative of tangy, sharper and more lively in flavour.

clue.text: Put note in box for dispenser

indicators.note: the musical note is put inside the box, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a chest is a large box
mi (or me) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone places a memo in a box for a pharmacist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispenser' is a pharmacist who dispenses medicines.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist makes up and hands out prescriptions, so dispensing drugs is the job.

clue.text: Undoubted vandal brought in to deal with the Hispaniola's quest

indicators.note: the two pieces are placed inside the phrase for dealing with something

parts.note: to treat a matter is to deal with it
undoubted means certain, sure
the Huns, like the Vandals, were barbarian invaders, so a destructive person is a Hun

explanation.surface: A certain vandal is called in to handle the voyage of a famous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hispaniola is the ship in Stevenson's Treasure Island, whose crew sail to find Flint's buried gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The voyage in Stevenson's novel is a search for buried pirate gold, a quest for hidden riches.

clue.text: Stun prisoner with some bad language…

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
a cuss is a swear word, a bit of bad language

explanation.surface: Knocking out a convict while swearing at him.
explanation.definitionFit: To concuss is to daze someone with a blow to the head.

clue.text: … being mostly the continental style

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: an entity is a being, something that exists
le is French for the, the continental word

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the continental style of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this to the previous clue for surface sense only; 'mostly' drops the final letter of the synonym for being, and 'style' is the verb, to name.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone a particular title is to designate or name them so, as in being called Lord.

clue.text: Leaders of Indian nations expect ruthless treatment still

indicators.note: the leading letter of each of the five words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Heads of Indian states anticipate harsh handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something motionless or inactive is not moving, still.

clue.text: Our money invested in port without a … without a smell

indicators.note: money invested is placed inside something, so one piece goes into the other
the port is taken without its letter, so that letter is removed

parts.note: Odessa is a Black Sea port in Ukraine
L stands for pound, money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Our cash is put into a harbour lacking something, which has no scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops the A of the Black Sea port; the shortened port then has 'invested in' it the word Our plus the pound sign. The second 'without a' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no scent at all, as fresh water or some gases are.

clue.text: Attentive old black man

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a man is a manservant

explanation.surface: An elderly dark-skinned person described as watchful.
explanation.definitionFit: Being watchful and quick to notice things means paying close attention.

clue.text: Spectre — he can produce a feeling of fear

indicators.note: the letters given can be made to produce something new by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A ghost is able to make one frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the shivers of unease or horror, the jitters.

clue.text: Pain of artist taken in by uninhibited teacher

indicators.note: the artist is enclosed inside the other piece
the teacher loses its outer letters, its inhibitions, leaving the middle

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter fooled by a free-spirited schoolteacher suffers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uninhibited' strips the outer letters of teacher, and 'taken in by' puts the Royal Academician inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the ear is a specific kind of pain.

clue.text: Painter beat girl up

parts.note: to rap is to strike or beat

indicators.note: in a down clue the girl's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Leah is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An artist assaults a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LEAH into HAEL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian Renaissance master who painted the School of Athens.

clue.text: Quail, a creature fierce at heart

parts.note: a cow is a farm creature

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word fierce are used

explanation.surface: A quail is described as a bird with a ferocious spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quail' looks like the bird but is the verb, to shrink back in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to flinch or shrink back in fear.

clue.text: Action about expression of dissatisfaction in the galley

indicators.note: the legal action goes round the jeer, enclosing it

parts.note: an action at law is a case
boo is a cry of disapproval

explanation.surface: A lawsuit about complaints in the ship's kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the galley' is a ship's kitchen rather than a rowing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: On old ships the cookhouse on deck was called by this name; in the US it also means a guard's van.

clue.text: Fighting over Scottish town — and. English one

indicators.note: in a down clue the fighting goes above, over, the Scottish town

parts.note: fighting is war
Wick is a town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland

explanation.surface: Battle over a town in Scotland, and over one in England too.
explanation.walkthrough: Wick is a small town in northern Scotland. 'English one' means an English town, Warwick, county town of Warwickshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwick is a county town in the English Midlands, famous for its castle.

clue.text: A rugby player — very large, by the way

parts.note: a prop is a forward in the front row of a rugby scrum
OS is short for outsize, the clothing label for very large

explanation.surface: A huge rugby forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means incidentally, introducing a remark on a related subject.

clue.text: Cyst is coming up from tendon

indicators.note: in a down clue both pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a wen is a cyst on the skin

explanation.surface: A cyst is developing on a tendon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns WEN plus IS, giving SINEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a cord of tissue joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Family in a short time rejected spiritual enlightenment

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole is read in reverse
the family is placed inside the short time

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour, a short time
a tribe is a family or clan

explanation.surface: A family quickly turned away from religious insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the family inside the hour, and 'rejected' turns the whole result backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born again, a spiritual renewal or awakening.

clue.text: Tie up mad canine gripping husband

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the husband inside them
something mad is crazy and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Restraining a rabid dog that has seized its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' turns CANINE into ENCAIN, and 'gripping' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind or fetter with chains, to tie someone up.

clue.text: A lie on a hazard affected by wind

indicators.note: to hazard is to chance or venture, so these letters take their chance in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A golf ball lies on a bunker, buffeted by the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hazard' looks like a golf bunker but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Aeolus, Greek god of the winds; an Aeolian harp sounds when wind blows over it.

clue.text: Give voice to a' cry of pain and run — a trait of cowardice

parts.note: to yell is to voice something loudly
ow is an exclamation of pain
to streak is to run very fast

explanation.surface: Shout out in agony and then flee like a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowardly streak in someone's character.
